8251fab7a9f4c561d24b5f088f3002d0070177e6.summary: Doctor Web, a Russian anti-virus company, reported on 22 August 2012 a backdoor it named Mac.BackDoor.Wirenet.1. It described it as the first cross-platform backdoor to run on both Linux and Mac OS X. The backdoor logs keystrokes and steals passwords stored by several browsers, mail clients and chat applications. It uses AES to communicate with its control server. The report did not yet say how it spreads. Doctor Web's products detect and remove it.

dates.what: Doctor Web reported the emergence of the first cross-platform backdoor for Linux and Mac OS X

82c459aa6c5ad1880851e4fcaed3a989434caf3a.summary: Malpedia family entry for RokRAT, described as a backdoor distributed as an encoded binary that is decrypted by shellcode after weaponized documents are exploited. It can capture screenshots, log keystrokes, evade analysis with anti-virtual machine checks and use cloud storage APIs. Most of the page is a dated list of third-party report titles from 2017 to 2025 that link RokRAT to APT37, ScarCruft and related groups.
